items.title: Radiohead Announce First Australian Tour in 15 Years With 16 Arena Shows
items.summary:
Radiohead will return to Australia in 2027 for a 16-show arena tour, their first dates in the country since 2012 and, the band says, their only concerts anywhere in the world next year outside a five-show run in Saitama, Japan. Thom Yorke, Jonny Greenwood, Colin Greenwood, Philip Selway and Ed O'Brien will play extended stands rather than a conventional national circuit, presented by Frontier Touring.

The tour opens with four nights at Perth's RAC Arena beginning May 3, then moves to six-show residencies at Melbourne's Rod Laver Arena from May 13 and Sydney's Afterpay Arena from May 25, closing June 1. Billboard reported that the band has confirmed no additional 2027 concerts elsewhere, making the Australian and Japanese dates the whole of the year's touring.

The run follows a series of European residency shows in late 2025, which were the group's first performances after several years off the road while its members worked on solo and side projects. Speculation about an Australian return had been circulating for months, helped along by O'Brien, who told Rolling Stone earlier this year, "We'd love to come to Australia. It's just a question of when."

Anticipating heavy demand, Frontier Touring will distribute both general and accessible tickets through a registration system instead of a first-come sale. Registration is open now and closes at 5 p.m. AEST on Thursday, Sept. 10, with the promoter saying every entry submitted inside that window will be weighted equally. Each ticket carries a $2 donation split between Greenpeace Australia Pacific and the Australian Marine Conservation Society.

The Oxford band broke through in 1993 with "Creep," still their highest-charting Billboard Hot 100 single at No. 34 and later certified platinum in the U.S. They have reached the Hot 100 only three times, the others being "High and Dry" and "Nude," but have topped the Billboard 200 four times, including with "Hail to the Thief," "In Rainbows" and 2016's "A Moon Shaped Pool," their most recent studio album. The six-time Grammy winners entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019.

items.title: Thanks to South Park, Trump Finally Got His Emmy
items.summary:
"South Park" won Outstanding Animated Program at Sunday night's Creative Arts Emmys, handing Trey Parker and Matt Stone a trophy for a season built largely around a caricature of Donald Trump. The winning stretch of Season 28 depicted the president as micro-endowed and, in one storyline, impregnating Satan.

Parker and Stone marked the win by releasing poster artwork of Trump holding the Emmy, captioned "You finally got your Emmy!" The joke lands on a long-running grievance: Trump spent years publicly complaining that "The Apprentice" had been snubbed by the Television Academy.

Consequence noted the irony that the award finally attached to Trump's name came by way of a show that spent a season mocking him. The Creative Arts Emmys precede the main Primetime Emmy ceremony, where the bulk of the series and performance categories are handed out.

items.title: Nathan Fielder Premieres Secret New Elizabeth Holmes Documentary
items.summary:
Nathan Fielder has made a documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, and he kept it quiet until the moment it screened. A24 premiered the film, titled "You Can See Everything," at the Telluride Film Festival on Sunday with virtually no advance notice, releasing a teaser trailer and poster online the same day.

Fielder co-directed with Lance Oppenheim, who is also behind "Primetime," A24's upcoming thriller drawn from the Chris Hansen "Dateline" segments. According to the official synopsis, the film begins 34 days before Holmes reports to prison, when the Theranos founder invites a skeptical crew to document her every move; what starts as a portrait of "an enigmatic felon" turns into "a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss."

Holmes founded the blood-testing company Theranos and was convicted of defrauding investors after raising close to $1 billion. A federal judge sentenced her to more than 11 years in prison in 2022.

Consequence reported that the documentary will get a wide release in October. It is Fielder's first project since the second season of "The Rehearsal" on HBO.

items.title: Summer U.S. Box Office Hits All-Time $4.76B Record: How Audiences Surrendered To Moviegoing
items.summary:
The summer domestic box office closed at a record $4.76 billion, a figure no one in the business was forecasting when the season began. Deadline reported that admissions rose along with grosses, citing EntTelligence data putting attendance above 322 million tickets against 275 million for summer 2025 — a direct rebuttal to the idea that revenue gains came purely from higher ticket prices.

Rentrak's numbers show it was the first summer on record in which all four core months cleared $1 billion each domestically: $1.07 billion in May, $1.08 billion in June, $1.18 billion in July and $1.276 billion in August. Lionsgate started it early, opening "Michael" the last weekend of April; the film became the studio's biggest ever at $372.3 million domestic and over $1 billion worldwide, drawing a crowd that was 30% Black, 30% Caucasian and 29% Hispanic and Latino, with 45% describing themselves as occasional moviegoers.

From there the majors staggered their tentpoles by audience rather than competing for the same one. "The Devil Wears Prada 2" drew a 75% female crowd and 56% infrequent moviegoers. Focus Features' "Obsession" opened to $17.1 million on May 15 but held with a near-$32 million four-day second weekend, and pulled 75% of its turnout from the 18-34 bracket.

Younger audiences showed up for specific titles: 55% of the crowd for A24's "Backrooms" was under 25, as was 51% for "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and 38% for "Obsession." "Backrooms" gave A24 its biggest opening ever at $81.4 million and its highest domestic total at $197.5 million, with filmmakers Kane Parsons and "Obsession" director Curry Barker both arriving from YouTube.

Not everything worked. Disney and Lucasfilm's "Star Wars: Mandalorian and Grogu" finished as the lowest-grossing live-action "Star Wars" film at $177.7 million domestic and $345.3 million worldwide against a $165 million production cost, though its $98 million four-day opening helped push Memorial Day weekend past $220 million.

Bill Skelly, head of Greenlight Analytics, said the pattern is holding into autumn. "We don't see the momentum stopping, the top 15 films we're tracking for the fall are running an average of 3.5 points ahead the average from the top 15 at the same point in time from last year," he said, adding that infrequent moviegoers were buying multiple tickets across the summer.

items.title: Macklemore Calls Out ‘Free Palestine’ Onstage, Spurring Petition Demanding He Leave Ed Sheeran Tour
items.summary:
Macklemore used his opening set for Ed Sheeran at MetLife Stadium on Friday night to sing out "Free Palestine" and then address the crowd directly, saying he wanted people in Gaza and the occupied West Bank to know they had not been forgotten. "I believe that every human being walking on this earth deserves exactly the same freedom," he told the audience. He repeated the remarks during Saturday night's show.

The Israeli American Council responded with a petition calling for Macklemore's removal from the remaining dates of Sheeran's Loop tour. "This was an Ed Sheeran concert — not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event," the petition reads. "The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda." Variety reported that the petition does not display a signature count.

The remarks are consistent with the rapper's public positions over the past two years. He released "Hind's Hall" in 2024, a song critical of Israel's actions in Gaza, and directed its proceeds to humanitarian work through UNRWA. He also criticized U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement during the MetLife sets.

Reaction from the stadium split along predictable lines on social media. Some attendees said they walked out because they had not expected a political rally and accused Macklemore of antisemitism, while others defended him, with one writing that "music has always been a vital platform for human rights advocacy, not just mindless escape." Neither Sheeran nor the tour has acted on the petition's demand, and Macklemore remains on the bill.
